historical_reviews.deepseek: The read operation is passive but the literal range cannot prove six sensors. It also does not distinguish PSU-internal temperature from a PDB connector/rail-zone probe or record PSU population/feed state.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly assigns critical power-safety context and excludes PMBus/power writes. This review adds per-bay serial/feed provenance and measurement-point semantics.
historical_reviews.duplicate_search: No duplicate code exists; adjacent FPGA and link-port chip sensors cannot provide PSU/PDB evidence.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-35 requires per-member range evidence, ED-36 makes fitted PSU topology and sensor meaning readiness inputs, and ED-38 preserves power/log state and engineer verdict ownership.

original_test_intent: Verify every applicable TEMP_PDB_PSU1–PSU6 thermal channel, including its PSU bay/feed and PDB measurement-point identity, readable value and enabled thresholds in raw IPMI and both BMC-Web views.
original_method: The power owner enumerates fitted PSU bays, feeds and corresponding PDB thermal points, maps each to exact SDR/Web records and supplies operating limits; automation gathers complete passive per-member evidence at a documented load state for operator confirmation.
manual_activity: The power/platform owner maps each fitted PSU1–PSU6 bay, serial and feed to its PDB sensor, defines whether the reading is PSU internal, connector or rail-zone temperature, supplies limits and confirms both Web entries.
required_inputs: Fitted PSU1–PSU6 bay/model/serial/firmware inventory and independent feed topology
PDB board revision, connector/rail-zone map and each sensor's physical measurement point
Exact per-member SDR name/record/entity and Dashboard/Server Health mapping
Units, scaling, tolerance, polling/freshness and absent/standby semantics
Expected range and enabled thresholds under documented load, redundancy and ambient state
BMC/SDR/PDB/PSU firmware and power-thermal specification revisions
Secret-safe OOB access, complete evidence retention and no-clear policy
PSU/PDB/rail thermal aborts and independent power/BMC recovery owner
safety_requirements: Enumerate exact PSU1–PSU6 members; do not execute the tilde range as one name
Bind every reading to a fitted bay, serial/feed and PDB measurement point
Do not substitute PSU status, power, voltage/current or internal PSU telemetry unless the approved map identifies it as this channel
Retain complete SDR and enabled threshold flags; no 100-line cap
Do not issue PMBus, PSU/power/feed, threshold, firmware, reset or log-clear commands
Stop on missing/stale/invalid sensor, feed/rail anomaly, unsafe temperature, threshold mismatch or management instability
Protect credentials and do not automatically retry
agent_execution_scope: Verify source identity and PSU/PDB/feed topology
Capture complete read-only SDR/Sensor inventory and exact results for all applicable members
Parse per-bay temperature, state, freshness and enabled thresholds
Build bay/feed/measurement-point parity and prepare both Web rows
Correlate passive PSU status, rails, load, SEL, fans and BMC health
Perform no PMBus/power/feed/threshold action or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve fitted PSU/PDB member and feed mapping
Define each measurement point, operating context and thresholds
Confirm both Web mappings and absent/standby handling
Review every member and issue the overall result

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Exact read-only queries will be useful after enumeration, but `'TEMP_PDB_PSU1~6'` is not six queries; the fallback is incomplete, credentials are exposed and no bay/feed/Web provenance is collected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Using secret-safe OOB access, retain the full SDR inventory and query each owner-mapped PDB/PSU temperature record separately, preserving threshold flags and load/feed context, then reconcile with both Web views.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: PSU1~6 scope, Dashboard and Server Health paths, reading/threshold criterion and 1/1-minute estimates remain; population, measurement points and limits are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a six-bay feed/measurement-point table, collect all exact passive records at a known load and redundancy state, and verify enabled thresholds across raw and both Web views.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces literal-range collection with power-topology-aware evidence and separates several possible meanings of PDB_PSU temperature.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One generic PSU read cannot cover six bay-specific PDB zones; aggregate PSU health or normal rail power does not prove local connector/controller temperature thresholds.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Readback is passive, but wrong bay or sensor attribution can hide overheating on a live high-current power path.

project_override_considerations: Unpopulated bays require explicit not-applicable entries. Shared sensors, redundant feeds or PDB revisions with different layouts need a versioned fan-out mapping rather than repeating one value across PSU indices.
expected_evidence: PSU1–PSU6 bay/model/serial/feed inventory and PDB revision
Per-member connector/rail-zone or internal measurement definition and SDR/Web identity
Value, units, state, freshness and enabled-threshold table under load/redundancy context
Complete redacted SDR plus exact member outputs with status/timestamps
Dashboard and Server Health screenshots/exports per member

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The row consistently requests six PDB/PSU temperature readings and Web thresholds. It lacks measurement-point definitions and values but provides no contradictory target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A passive six-member PDB/PSU thermal check is identifiable. Population, topology, sensor semantics and thresholds are supplyable project inputs under ED-36.

review_improvement: Turns an ambiguous range into a bay/feed/measurement-point matrix, preserves power safety and prevents status or rail telemetry from substituting for the requested local temperatures.
independent_technical_reasoning: `PDB_PSU` can plausibly refer to a PSU's internal reading, a PDB-side connector probe or a rail-zone sensor, and those locations have different limits and fault implications. Bay serial/feed attribution is essential because a normal value on one redundant path cannot cover another. Complete read-only evidence at known load can validate all six without manipulating live power.
